coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Genentech Hall
record.summary: UCSF's first Mission Bay building, opened in 2003 at 600 16th St, housing programs in structural and chemical biology, molecular, cell and developmental biology, and the Molecular Design Institute.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against DataSF's Assessor parcel data and tax roll -- e.g. blklot 8711507 at 675 Mission Bay Blvd alone is ~12.2 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.

facts.value: Programs in structural and chemical biology, molecular, cell and developmental biology, the Molecular Design Institute, the Center for Advanced Technology, a library, an auditorium and commercial space

costs.what: Total capital-improvement budget the UC Regents amended and approved in March 1999 for 'UC Hall Seismic Replacement, Mission Bay' (Building 24) -- believed to be this building based on matching gross square footage (433,828 gsf) and programs, per the January 2000 Regents item that recounts the March 1999 action; the March 1999 item itself does not use the 'Genentech Hall' name

milestones.text: UC Regents approve an amended $222.4 million capital-improvement budget, funding plan, environmental documentation and design for the 'UC Hall Seismic Replacement, Mission Bay' project (Building 24) -- believed to be this building based on matching gross square footage (433,828 gsf) and programs (structural/chemical biology, molecular/cell/developmental biology), per a January 2000 Regents item recounting the March 1999 action; site preparation began October 1999 and steel-frame construction began December 1999, per the same January 2000 item

changes.text: Genentech Hall's January 2003 opening month came from a page that could not be re-read; the opening is now dated 2003, as UCSF's own history page gives it.

The '303-acre campus' wording was dropped (that is the whole Mission Bay area; UCSF's history and Clark describe a 43-acre campus), the programs housed now follow UCSF's history page (structural and chemical biology, molecular, cell and developmental biology, the Molecular Design Institute) rather than 'biochemistry, biophysics', and the unsupported 'San Francisco office' for SmithGroup was removed. Size and story-count facts now also cite UCSF's history and Clark. The parcel note now gives 675 Mission Bay Blvd at about 12.2 acres, and a dated note says the tax-roll claim for 600 16th St is unsupported (the parcel is addressed 1700 4th St). The Block 24A/B label now cites UCSF's June 2025 CAC map. The 2008 photo no longer carries a 'taken' date because the source dates only the presentation, and the Wikimedia photo credit no longer names an author or a flight the file page does not state. The January 2003 opening and 'first building' claims rest on a Tradeline article that could not be read and were left in place.

open_questions: Exact opening day is sourced only to a first-researcher-moved-in anecdote (Jan 8, 2003) and a February 2003 trade-press 'now open' piece, not an official UCSF dedication date -- recorded as month-level, approximate.
Square footage varies 400,000-435,000 sq ft across sources; not resolved to one authoritative figure.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

Images: the only photograph found of Genentech Hall is undated beyond appearing in a September 2008 UC Regents presentation slide (shared with its neighbor); its exact capture date isn't confirmed. No site plan or architectural rendering specific to this building was found in a public-record source.

As of 2026-09-21, the March 1999 Regents budget/design approval for 'UC Hall Seismic Replacement, Mission Bay (Building 24)' is identified as this building's likely earlier stage, via a January 2000 Regents item that recounts it and gives 433,828 gsf (matching this record's own 400,000-435,000 range). The March 1999 item itself was not retrieved directly; the January 2000 item's own recap is the source used.

As of 2026-09-29, the Tradeline article (source of 'January 2003', 'first Mission Bay building' and the five stories) could not be re-checked; UCSF's history page confirms only the 2003 opening and 'more than 400,000 gross square feet', and Clark gives '435,000-square-foot, five-story' (sidebar: 415,000). The earlier '303-acre campus' wording was dropped: 303 acres is the whole Mission Bay redevelopment area, while UCSF's history and Clark describe a 43-acre campus. The 2008 Regents slide dates the presentation, not the photograph, so the image's 'taken' date was removed.
